newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet likely to debate PBK sale next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet likely to debate PBK sale next week.

text.p: The Polish government is likely to discuss the privatisation of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) at its session next week, the government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said on Tuesday.
"This point was dropped from today's agenda. It will probably be discussed at the government's next session," Jakubowska told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

The choice of an investor for 10 to 65 percent of PKB has been delayed for weeks, with June 12 the most recent target date missed. The government plans to float another 15 percent of the bank on the Warsaw bourse.
The treasury ministry's adviser in the bank's privatisation, HSBC Investment Services, said on Tuesday that PBK's issue prospectus would be submitted to the Securities Commission by Wednesday.
"The bank's public offer will be possible in October," Hubert Janiszewski, president of HSBC's Polish unit, told Reuters.
Polish and international firms are bidding for PBK.
A consortium of Polish Development Bank (PBR), Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH), Kredyt Bank and insurer Warta has confirmed it was bidding for at least 51 percent of PBK.
Earlier this month the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said it was willing to buy up to 15 percent of the bank.
Samsung Life Insurance, a subsidiary of South Korea's Samsung, has also expressed interest in buying a PBK stake.
HSBC Investment Services has estimated PBK's total value at between 1.2 billion and 1.6 billion zlotys. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
